thread:
Sam: Kicking off a small canary for cypress11b-int4 on the littoral pool. Goal: validate latency/cost and watch for mem-frag OOMs. Starting with batch=1, max_new_tokens=384, prefetch=off.
Alyssa: Nice. Can you add a perf trace tag so we can correlate kv churn? e.g. ?trace=cypress11b-canary1
Sam: Yep — added trace tag. Deploy shows warmstart succeeded for two nodes, then one task hit a CUDA OOM during generation step 2.
Devon: ugh. Got the stack from the failed run, paste below:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 29.40 GiB already allocated; 128.00 MiB free; 2.12 GiB cached)
  at inference.py:generate_batch()
  at serving/runtime/kv_cache.cpp:evict_slot()
```
Devon: Appears to be fragmentation — a nominally small allocation failed because free chunks are scattered.
Maria: Are we using per-request max_new_tokens fallback? Canary config had 384 hard-coded. Maybe when clients send long prompts + 384 it blows past expectation.
Sam: Good call. I see a spike: one request had input_len=3k tokens then generated 384 -> sequence 3384. Kernel selection for longer sequences moves to slower gemm path and allocs grow.
Luca: Two immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) enforce soft cap: if input_len + max_new_tokens > 2048, cap max_new_tokens to 128; 2) enable early KV eviction for int4 variants (evict oldest prefixes when slot usage > 0.85).
Alyssa: Also worth trying reducing default max_new_tokens for canary to 256 and enabling compaction on warmstart (slot compactor every 30s). Has helped in other int4 rigs.
Sam: I'll roll changes in this order: set default max_new_tokens=256, enable slot compactor(t=30s), set canary batch=1 -> still same. If OOM persists, switch to prefetch=on for small batches to stabilize memory layout.
Devon: I'll run a memory-defrag trace (mem-prof) across the failing node to get heatmap of allocations. If fragmentation shows many small temporary tensors, we can try reserving a transient buffer (heap_shrink tweak) to force larger contiguous free ranges.
Maria: On the quality front: quantization mapping looks ok but we should run our eval harness (qa/bench-llm) at both 256 and 384 max_new_tokens to check for any generation regressions after soft-capping. I'll queue that.
ops-bot: Canary deployed to dedicated-1 (nodes: d1-03,d1-07). Monitoring: infra.latency_p50=210ms, mem.free_p50=1.1GiB, errors=1 (OOM).
Alyssa: If memory trace indicates heavy KV churn, we might try a hybrid strategy: move larger key/value tensors to pinned arena (reduce scatter) and bias kernel selection toward int8 GEMM for long sequences. But that requires a quick quant sanity run.
Sam: Quick experiment plan (short):
- Step 1 (now): set canary defaults -> max_new_tokens=256, slot_compactor=30s, early_kv_eviction=0.85
- Step 2 (30m): run mem-prof + generate 10 long prompts (3k tokens) to repro
- Step 3 (1h): run eval harness at 256 vs 384 to check quality deltas
- Step 4 (if still OOM): reduce batch_safety_threshold and enable prefetch=on for canary only; add transient-reserve=512MiB
Devon: I'll own Step 2 and collect heap histograms. Sam can patch canary config. Maria will run evals.
Maria: On schedule. If we see >2% BLEU/QA regressions at 256, escalate to model-ops to consider re-quant (per-layer scale) or roll back canary.
Sam: Patch pushed for defaults. Deploying now.
Luca: FYI we already have a small rollout doc in runbooks/ml-frag (link) — follow the compaction + reserve pattern in section 2.2.
Sam: Thanks all. Will update thread with mem-prof results in ~45m. :thumbsup:
